PHYSICS / TEACHING / AI

Bingkun Qi — Physics · Teaching · AI

I'm Bingkun Qi, a science teacher at an international school, teaching physics, mathematics and advanced mathematics.

My studies and research have taken me to Fudan University, CUNY, Peking University and EPFL, with a research focus on non-Hermitian photonics. I also hold a Master of Engineering, Computing and Technology from Arizona State University.

From physics research to the classroom, I enjoy breaking complex problems into steps that people can understand and explore. I am also experimenting with AI-assisted development, turning everyday teaching needs into question banks and practice websites.

Interactive physics

Explore mechanics, waves and circuits: change the parameters, observe the results, and connect equations with physical behavior.

12 experiment topics · Chinese & English · Aligned with CAIE 9702 AS · Predict → Explore → Explain

01 / Waves · 9702 8.1.1

Wave superposition ↗

Change amplitude and phase to explore reinforcement and cancellation.

02 / Waves · 9702 8.1

Stationary waves ↗

Find nodes and antinodes, and explore harmonics on a string with fixed ends.

03 / Waves · 9702 8.3

Double-slit interference ↗

Vary wavelength, slit separation and screen distance to explore fringe spacing.

04 / Mechanics · 9702 2.1

Motion & graphs ↗

Connect a cart’s motion with graph gradients, signed areas and direction.

05 / Mechanics · 9702 3.3

Collisions & conservation ↗

Adjust masses and velocities to compare momentum and kinetic energy before and after impact.

06 / Circuits · 9702 10.3

Potential dividers & sensors ↗

Change light, temperature and sensor position to investigate the output voltage.

07 / Mechanics · 9702 2.1.9

Projectile motion ↗

Change the launch conditions and compare horizontal and vertical motion along the trajectory.

08 / Circuits · 9702 10.1

EMF & internal resistance ↗

Change the load resistance and compare current, terminal voltage and internal resistance.

09 / Mechanics · 9702 3.2

Drag & terminal velocity ↗

Compare weight, drag and speed as the resultant force approaches zero.

10 / Materials · 9702 6.1–6.2

Stretching & Young modulus ↗

Change the stretching conditions and compare force–extension and stress–strain relationships.

11 / Mechanics · 9702 5.1–5.2

Work & energy ↗

Compare work done by forces with changes in kinetic energy and follow the energy transfers.

12 / Waves · 9702 8.2

Diffraction through a slit ↗

Vary wavelength and slit width to compare how much the wave spreads beyond the opening.

Full experiments open in the separate lab with its existing access permissions.
